title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time around Mercer University and Macon.

cards.title: See contemporary art at the MAC
cards.subtitle: Downtown Macon
cards.notes: Visit during public gallery hours and spend time with the current exhibition; Mercer documents that admission and programming are free and open.
cards.short_summary: A Mercer-run contemporary-art gallery with free public admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer states that the McEachern Art Center offers free, open programming and admission.
cards.access_notes: Public gallery access; confirm exhibition hours before going.

cards.title: Browse the monthly gallery exhibits
cards.subtitle: 456 First St., downtown Macon
cards.notes: Drop in during listed gallery hours to view local artists’ rotating exhibits. Keep the visit focused on the free gallery rather than paid classes or purchases.
cards.short_summary: Downtown local-art exhibitions with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon states that The 567 Center features monthly local-art exhibits with free admission.
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours are listed as Monday–Friday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; classes and artwork purchases cost extra.

cards.title: Walk the mounds and Earth Lodge area
cards.subtitle: 1207 Emery Highway, Macon
cards.notes: Follow the open visitor routes, take in the Great Temple Mound, and visit the Earth Lodge during visitor-center hours; respect all site-protection rules.
cards.short_summary: Ancient Indigenous sites and walking routes in Macon’s national park.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states there is no fee to visit the park except during two special events.
cards.access_notes: The park and visitor facilities have separate hours; special events may be exceptions to free entry.

cards.title: Walk the river-bluff trails
cards.subtitle: 2551 North Pierce Drive, Macon
cards.notes: Use the marked trails for a low-key group walk and pause at overlooks. The listing identifies seven miles of trails and says park entry is free.
cards.short_summary: A free riverside park with wooded trails and overlooks.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon lists Amerson River Park as free and describes seven miles of trails.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are daily, with daylight-savings hours of 7:30 a.m.–8 p.m.; paid pavilion rentals are separate.

cards.title: Catch a free public movie screening
cards.subtitle: 1155 College Street, across from Mercer
cards.notes: Watch the park’s public-event notices and bring a blanket or chair when a screening is scheduled. The activity is the documented free public movie program.
cards.short_summary: A Mercer-adjacent park that hosts free public movie screenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon states that Tattnall Square Park is a spot for free public movie screenings.
cards.access_notes: Free screenings are event-based rather than daily; use the park’s current event notice for date details.

cards.title: Take a riverside walk or ride
cards.subtitle: Macon riverfront trail system
cards.notes: Pick a daylight section for walking, biking, or birdwatching with friends. The trail is described as a recreational resource linking riverfront parks and history.
cards.short_summary: A riverside trail system for low-key outdoor recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon identifies the Ocmulgee Heritage Trail as a place for walking, biking, boating, and birdwatching, and states Macon parks are all free.
cards.access_notes: Use publicly accessible trail sections and follow posted trail conditions and rules.

cards.title: Follow the illuminated architecture route
cards.subtitle: Historic intown Macon
cards.notes: Take the self-guided evening walk at your own pace, staying on public sidewalks and admiring the lit façades from outside rather than entering private homes.
cards.short_summary: A free, self-guided nighttime architecture stroll.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon describes Lights on Macon as a free self-guided tour available 365 nights a year.
cards.access_notes: Self-guided outdoor route; observe traffic, sidewalks, and private-property boundaries.

cards.title: Meet up for an off-leash dog play session
cards.subtitle: 831 Adams Street, Macon
cards.notes: Bring a dog only if you can supervise it and follow posted rules. The documented no-fee option is a simple outdoor meetup for dog owners and friends.
cards.short_summary: A free Macon dog park for supervised play and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon calls Macon Dog Park a free place where dogs and owners can run free.
cards.access_notes: Bring a supervised dog and follow posted park rules; this activity is optional for visitors without a dog.

cards.title: Pause for a riverfront park walk
cards.subtitle: 301 Riverside Drive, Macon
cards.notes: Use this named Ocmulgee Heritage Trail-area park for a short outdoor reset or a walking meetup, following posted rules and choosing daylight hours.
cards.short_summary: A named Macon park along the riverfront trail network.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon lists Gateway Park and states that Macon’s parks are all free.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-park use only; check local conditions and posted rules before visiting.

cards.title: Plan a no-cost park meetup
cards.subtitle: Macon, Georgia
cards.notes: Meet for a walk, conversation, or an outdoor break in this named city park. Keep plans simple and use public areas in line with any posted regulations.
cards.short_summary: A free Macon public-park option for an outdoor hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon identifies Central City Park within Macon’s park network and states that parks are all free.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-park use; consult posted notices for any event-specific restrictions.
